reviewer: Claude (fresh independent reviewer; no author claims used as evidence)
verdictSummary: Candidate03 is a large, largely sound correction. The frozen closure copy passes its own strict checker. Fit parity is now a pinned, disclosed first page, and the ledger, history and slot policies exist. Independent subject3 and static-parity recomputation agree, and the metadata-v2 acceptance bytes are unchanged. Six findings remain: two blocking and four required. (1) A complete owner graph page can still be silently cut and admitted as complete-page-set by relabelling countBasis lower-bound. (2) The budget does not bound owner-valid maxima of mandatory root metadata: a join-consistent failure report with 323 B of panels is refused CODEC-BYTES because the root allowance was derived from a placeholder. The required findings are: renderer failure can replace a query refusal, and cancellation/interrupted is unhandled (the model crashes); fresh-source closure is broken through the unhooked historical checker subprocess, including pyc consultation; the coverage overlay hides a real fit-row metadata drift behind a pre-existing first failure; and the F01-F10 obligations plus the R03 duration requirement lack any closure path, so approved functionality is unavailable indefinitely.

requiredFindings.title: A complete owner graph page can be silently cut and admitted as complete-page-set by setting countBasis lower-bound
evidence: Probe G1 (work/probes/probe_rpr3.json): audit-full slot 0, a 100-row owner page. It is relabelled traversalCoverage complete with the cursor removed, continuation complete-page-set, countBasis lower-bound, and items cut to 1; totalItems stays 107. admit_document returns accept.

check.py:434 applies the count join only when countBasis == 'exact': `need(cursor is None and (rctx['countBasis'] != 'exact' or rctx['totalItems'] == len(items)), 'J-GRAPH-COUNT')`. The same escape exists at :436 for truncated-page.

Owner law: query-projection-contract.v3.md:140 'Completeness is traversalCoverage=complete and countBasis=exact'; :136 lower-bound only for produced-prefix remaining owed work; graph-query.schema.json CountBasis description.
Controls: the same slice with countBasis exact gives J-GRAPH-COUNT (G3); relabelled truncated-bound gives J-GRAPH-CONTINUATION (G2).

Root decision violated: 'never slice owner response without accurate context/cursors'. Graph provenance claims 'page-count-and-continuation-joins' is verifiedInDocument (build_owner.py PROVENANCE.graph).
requiredFindings.correction: Enforce the owner completeness law: complete implies countBasis exact and totalItems == len(items). lower-bound requires a truncated coverage with producedItems == totalItems >= items. Refuse complete-page-set on any non-exact or truncated-bound answer. Add G1 and its truncated-page variant as refusal cases with a stable code.

requiredFindings.title: The report budget does not bound owner-valid maxima of mandatory root metadata; the root allowance is derived from a placeholder
evidence: build_owner.py:391-392 worst_root_bytes uses `purgeDisclosure: {placeholder: wide*1024}`. The owner PinnedPurgeDisclosure allows activePins maxItems 4096 with pinId maxLength 256 (common.schema.json #/$defs/PinnedPurgeDisclosure), and the StepTermination evidence.pinned branch is legal on any step (common.schema.json StepTermination allOf).

Probe L1: the largest owner-valid StepTermination within the 4 MiB owner codec is 4,193,710 B (3982 pins; schema- and codec-valid). The author's worst root is 871,329 B and rootAllowanceBytes is 917,504 (contract.md:238).

Probe B1 (work/probes/probe_budget_coverage.json): an audit failure report (kind=failure, all panels no-admitted-result, 323 panel bytes). The envelope is at its boundary (4,194,016 B) and every recorded required step (3) is rejected with an owner-valid 2,096,965 B pinned termination; all ledger joins are consistent. It is refused CODEC-BYTES at 10,489,377 B > documentMaxBytes 9,306,112. The control with one large step is accepted at 6,295,587 B.

The byte law (report_model.py project_exploration) fills panels to 4 MiB independently of root size, so any root above the allowance plus a boundary envelope plus full panels also exceeds documentMaxBytes.
The ledger is mandatory (required root member; ledger-omitted gives SCHEMA). The only outcome is delivery failure (contract.md:269), which then replaces the invocation's own termination (see RPR3-3).
requiredFindings.correction: Derive the root allowance from owner maxima that the joins actually permit: recorded steps are bounded by the inventory5 steps per HTML command (at most 4), each carrying a max-codec termination. Alternatively represent ledger terminations that are byte-equal to the envelope termination by reference, or bound ledger termination bytes with an explicit owned projection (for example domainDetail digest plus a disclosure of omission). Make the byte law budget against (documentMaxBytes - envelope - root) rather than a fixed 4 MiB. Add B1 as an accepted or typed-boundary case, and state the delivery outcome for over-cap mandatory metadata.

requiredFindings.title: D9 aggregate: a renderer failure can replace a query refusal, and cancellation/interrupted is unrepresented (admission crashes)
evidence: (a) contract.md:103-104: 'Only a real renderer failure is DELIVERY.RENDERER_FAILED_AFTER_COMMIT, and D9 ordering then applies as owned.' Probe D1: report_model.d9_aggregate([analysis success, query request-rejected, render operational-failed RENDERER_FAILED_AFTER_COMMIT]) returns operational-failed / RENDERER_FAILED_AFTER_COMMIT, so the query refusal is replaced. fixtures aggregateCases cover only an operational tie (fit-query-io-then-renderer-io-tie-keeps-first-detail). The report-only refusal ledger-renderer-failure-overrides-query-refusal holds only because the render step is never recorded in a report (check.py:327); json/human/agent envelopes have no such law or golden. The root decision is 'renderer failure cannot replace query failure'.

(b) report_model.py:32 D9_ORDER omits interrupted. Probe D2: an owner-valid recorded step termination {class interrupted, signal SIGINT} makes admit_document raise UNCAUGHT ValueError ('list.index(x): x not in list') instead of a typed refusal or acceptance.

InvocationLedgerV1 omits InvocationRecord.cancellation (invocation-record.schema.json root properties; Cancellation.phase), so the owned before-settle 'aggregate is interrupted (130)' and after-settle 'not reclassified' laws (workflows-and-surfaces.md:224-228) cannot be recomputed by J-LEDGER-AGGREGATE.
requiredFindings.correction: (a) State and golden the query-refusal plus renderer-failure outcome for every fit renderer, consistent with the root decision (for example the query step termination stands and renderer failure is disclosed separately), or record a root decision adopting D9 dominance. (b) Carry cancellation in the ledger, implement the owned cancellation aggregate, and add interrupted before-settle and after-settle report cases.

requiredFindings.title: Fresh-source closure is bypassed by the unhooked historical checker subprocess, including architecture pyc consultation
evidence: check.py:899 runs `subprocess.run([PY, '-I', '-B', check_metadata.py, ...])` outside the audit hook, without a pycache prefix. contract.md:316 claims only that the child 'verifies its own pins'.

Whole-process trace of that exact child (work/probes/trace-summary.json child) shows governed opens not in source-pins.json: foundation/__pycache__/canonical.cpython-314.pyc, workflows/command-inventory.v3.json, metadata-v2/README.md, metadata-v2/successor.json (the child's own pin anchor), v2/architecture/implementation-boundaries-and-build-plan.md, implementation-coverage.v1.json and repository-file-inventory.v1.json, plus the unpinned listing docs/implementation/m1/metadata-v2.

Probe work/probes/pyc_demo.out: under `-I -B` (dont_write_bytecode true, pycache_prefix None), spec_from_file_location on a hash-verified source executed an adjacent header-matched __pycache__ bytecode ('stale-bytecode'). check_metadata.load hash-checks canonical.py and then loads it exactly this way. The current architecture pyc headers do not match (mtime/size), so it is not live today, but the closure does not exclude it.
Parent process: trace shows 73 of 73 governed opens pinned, no unpinned listing, and pyc lookups only under /nonexistent-opensip-report-projection-pycache (sound).
requiredFindings.correction: Run the historical checker in-process under the hook with the same pycache_prefix, or launch it with `-X pycache_prefix=<nonexistent>` and a child-side hook. Pin the child's complete observed closure (the six files and the listing above) in source-pins.json, and assert that the child's closure trace equals the pins.

requiredFindings.title: The coverage overlay hides a real fit command-row metadata drift behind the pre-existing first validator failure
evidence: check.py:937-944 accepts the overlay when validate_coverage raises the same first message for base and overlay ('Missing/extra module milestone prerequisite'). validate_coverage stops at check_implementation_planning.py:103-105, before every per-row check (:107-150).

Probe C1: after neutralising only that pre-existing key-set condition (adding crates/reporting/src/assets.rs to moduleFirstMilestone for both), base returns 'valid' and the overlay returns 'Command metadata drift'.

Probe C2: the overlay fit commands row keeps parityFields [run-id, candidates, evidence-levels, termination-class, capability-availability], while inventory5 has 9 (the four candidates-* disclosure fields are missing). check_implementation_planning.py:145-147 requires equality. The row source digest was updated, but the row's own metadata was not.
requiredFindings.correction: Update the overlay fit row metadata (parityFields). Validate the overlay with the owned validator with only the pre-existing condition isolated, or compare the full ordered error sets, and assert that no new violation exists.

requiredFindings.title: F01-F10 obligations and R03 duration give approved report functionality no closure path, so it is unavailable indefinitely; design readiness is not separated from implementation
evidence: fixtures.json#/obligations RP-OBL-F01..F10 are bare absence statements with no owning design unit, lane, milestone, gate or closure criterion. contract.md:278 lists them as 'Feature owner absences'. FeatureStateV1.state is const 'unavailable' and featureStates are exact per-command consts (build_owner.py:423-426), with no successor or retirement path stated.
Probe C3: the reportFeatures coverage rows R05/R06/R07/R08/R12/R23 (M4) all verify 'including explicit feature states where an owner is absent', so showing the absence satisfies the planned test.

Requirements affected (prototype-report-inventory.md): R05 Preserve 'Show selected policy/capability descriptions' (:55; F01, F08); R06 Preserve 'descriptions, selectors and applicable parameters' (:61; F06, F07); R07 Change 'Bind metrics and test reachability' (:67; F09, F10); R08 Change directional package coupling (:73; F03); R12 Change host-projected bounded path with recognition evidence (:97; F05); R23 Change input/configuration disclosure (:165; F04). F02 is conditional ('Any historical run statistics', :55) and is acceptable as unavailable.

F03 (native unit membership exists, no query carrier) and F05 (FrameworkRecognitionV1.entryPoints exists, not retained) are design decisions within existing owners (query and retention), not absent owners. They are design-readiness items, not implementation lanes.

R03 requires 'typed outcomes and duration separately from verdict' (prototype-report-inventory.md:43). invocation:3 has no duration/timestamp field (only test-execution.schema.json durationMillis), and the report has no feature state or obligation for duration. The requirement vanishes silently, as in the RPR-4 class.
requiredFindings.correction: For each F obligation record: the owning design unit, whether it is a design blocker keeping AUDIT-G10 open (at least F03 and F05) or a root-recorded deferral, its target milestone and gate, and the successor path that retires the feature state (report-projection major or conditional member). Add a duration feature state and obligation, or a ledger duration carrier if an owner is selected. Change the reportFeatures verification so an absence does not satisfy delivery.

advisories.text: Slot selection can be steered by the host-asserted descriptor-not-retained state. Probe S1: marking the first retained subject not-retained re-plans slots [neighborhood,neighborhood,package-coupling,neighborhood,reach,path] to [neighborhood,package-coupling,neighborhood,reach,path], and the document is accepted (check.py:413-418, report_model.py:108-111). This is disclosed but not provable; consider requiring retention for subjects of findings on a sealed Run, or disclosing a not-retained count in the static section.

History count is host-controlled. Probe H1: understating priorRunsInSnapshot and dropping the oldest selected prior Run is accepted (check.py:511-512). 'selection-count-recomputed-from-snapshot-count' is arithmetic over a host number; name it that way.

The documented `--out` fails whenever the path is under /tmp/opensip-implementation outside the subject: the checker's own hook raises UNPINNED-LOAD at check.py:1039 after all checks pass. Writing inside the subject breaks the next --subject-strict run. Exempt the declared output path or write to stdout only.
Graph provenance verifiedInDocument 'page-count-and-continuation-joins' overclaims until RPR3-1 is fixed.

The contract (section 7) does not state that the baseline source Run is excluded from prior Runs; report_model.history_selection excludes it (:243) and admission relies on requestedRunIds uniqueItems. State it so that two hosts agree.

The hook refuses unpinned listing paths but does not re-digest a listing at use (check.py:127-131). Pins are verified once before import, so modification between verification and a later open (TOCTOU) is not detected. The docstring's 'drifted directory listing' refusal is start-time only.

R14 is titled 'Exact historical run selection beyond recent history' (prototype-report-inventory.md:107-109). The fixed policy selects the baseline source plus the most recent prior Runs and offers no explicit older-run selection or feature state. Root should confirm that this satisfies R14.

The architecture checkout holds stale pyc files for canonical.py and check_implementation_planning.py (headers currently mismatched). Any -I -B tool without a pycache prefix would consult them; see RPR3-4.
Generator compatibility (object/array consts, allOf narrowing) remains unexercised (RP-OBL-G01); no generator claim is made here.
